messages:
marta: Customer (acme-prod) opened a high-priority ticket: private inference endpoint returning 502s from their app subnet only. Works from our test subnet. Repro steps attached, need quick triage.

raj: Can you paste the minimal repro and VPC details? I can run a packet trace.

marta: Repro (from their app host):
```
curl -v https://inference.internal-acme:443/api/v1/generate --resolve inference.internal-acme:443:10.2.3.8
* About to connect() to 10.2.3.8 port 443
*   Trying 10.2.3.8... connected.
* Connected to 10.2.3.8 (10.2.3.8) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established, but no response body, then connection reset
* Received HTTP error 502 from proxy
```
Short tcpdump from their NAT instance (client IP 172.31.20.45 -> server 10.2.3.8):
```
10:01:12.123456 IP 172.31.20.45.54321 > 10.2.3.8.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240
10:01:12.125000 IP 10.2.3.8.443 > 54.210.11.22.32768: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```
They say the RST appears from an unexpected public IP (54.210.11.22) which is their NAT EIP.

kevin: Two quick guesses: 1) NACL or firewall is blocking ephemeral return ports on the path back (NACLs are stateless so need both directions open), 2) SNAT on the NAT gateway/NAT instance is rewriting to an ephemeral port that isn't allowed by a restrictive NACL/iptables rule.

raj: Exactly. The tcpdump shows client SYN to server:443, but server SYN/ACK likely gets to the NAT/EIP then translated to a different ephemeral port (32768) and gets dropped or RSTed because the NACL doesn't permit that inbound. Can you share the NACL rules and SG on the NAT subnet? Also check if source/dest check was disabled on a NAT instance.

marta: NACL for their app subnet (nacl-0a1b2c3d): inbound allows 443 from 10.2.0.0/16, outbound allows 443 to 10.2.0.0/16 only. SG on inference node (sg-0ff1a2b3) allows inbound 443 from vpc cidr and outbound 443 to 0.0.0.0/0.

kevin: There's the problem — outbound NACL for the app subnet is too restrictive. When the NAT rewrites source to the EIP and uses an ephemeral port (>=1024), the return path needs ephemeral ports allowed inbound on that subnet's NACL. NACLs are stateless so you must explicitly allow ephemeral ranges in both inbound/outbound directions. For AWS, allow 1024-65535 (or 32768-61000 depending on OS) as necessary. Alternatively place NAT in subnet with permissive NACL or switch to AWS-managed NAT gateway (stateful at VPC edge).

raj: Diagnostic commands to run on their NAT instance/NAT gateway VPC flow logs:
```
sudo tcpdump -n "host 172.31.20.45 and port 443" -w /tmp/trace.pcap
# check conntrack on NAT instance (if not gateway):
sudo conntrack -L | grep 172.31.20.45
# quick test after changing NACL:
curl -v --interface 172.31.20.45 https://inference.internal-acme:443
```

marta: I asked them to temporarily open ephemeral range 1024-65535 on NACL (both inbound & outbound) and to allow established return traffic on their perimeter firewall. They tested and the call now succeeds from their app subnet.

kevin: Nice. For follow-up: recommend documenting recommended NACL and SG templates for private inference customers (we should include NAT/gateway notes). Also remind customers that NACLs are stateless.

marta: I'll log the fix with the customer and update the support KB. Ticket closed pending postmortem. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Support ticket #ACME-3489 updated: customer confirmed workaround, plan to apply permanent NACL change in staging tomorrow.
